response.markdown_report:
**Proposed direction: calibrate diagnostic detection before interpreting activation patches.** At 20% progress, a small fault-injection calibration offers a practical next step without changing the single NextItNet predictor.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Movies and CDs show positive old-minus-random replacement contrasts. These indicate lower disruption from older substitutions, not harmful older history. (2) Electronics has a 9.38% negative-over-positive training ranking rate. This motivates investigation but does not establish weak validation HR@10. (3) Current controls cover several implementation properties, while export parity remains unverified. Diagnostic coverage therefore needs demonstrated detection and measured false alarms.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [DeepCrime](https://zenodo.org/records/5082873) motivates faults grounded in implementation mistakes. Diagnostic-only mutations can test whether the adapter detects such mistakes. (2) [Zhang and Nanda](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=Hf17y6u9BC) show that patching conclusions depend on corruption and outcome choices. Calibration should precede mechanistic interpretation. (3) [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establish limitations of sampled ranking metrics. Training diagnostic ranks must remain separate from host validation selection.

These insights define three directions: implementation detection, intervention reliability, and evaluation scope. The framework is **known fault → observable witness → diagnostic alarm → permitted interpretation**; natural-model patch effects remain exploratory evidence.

| Atomic idea | Originality / potential / difficulty | Positive; negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| A. Calibrate probes with isolated diagnostic mutations [DeepCrime] | 4 / 7 / 4 | Originality: targeted NextItNet integration; established mutation testing. Potential: exposes blind spots; artificial faults cover limited failures. Difficulty: reuses frozen weights; fault reachability needs care. |
| B. Add hybrid-activation distance checks [Zhang–Nanda] | 4 / 6 / 5 | Originality: architecture-specific transfer; familiar outlier checks. Potential: flags patch artifacts; normal distances cannot certify validity. Difficulty: bounded activation caching; reference selection is delicate. |
| C. Compare permitted sampled and full-catalog diagnostic ranks [Krichene–Rendle] | 3 / 6 / 5 | Originality: useful integration; established comparison. Potential: reveals candidate dependence; cannot replace pinned evaluation. Difficulty: straightforward scoring; catalog scans cost time. |

**Select A.** Keep one frozen NextItNet checkpoint per category and apply three temporary diagnostic mutations separately: incorrect `count−1` readout, explicit future-feature mixing, and constant history features. Each needs a demonstrable behavioral witness before detection is assessed. Unchanged execution and identity hooks provide negative controls.

Cache bounded training examples, preserve original final occupied readout and candidates, and record a fault-by-probe detection matrix, false alarms, localization where labels are defined, and unavailable cases. Predeclare tolerances and cap total calibration within the existing category diagnostic budget. Restore every temporary modification in `finally`.

Calibration measures toolkit sensitivity to specified injected faults. It neither certifies the unmodified model nor establishes current user demand. Preserve the adapter interfaces, all four routes, fixed seeds and training limits; host macro validation HR@10 remains the sole selection criterion.

idea.description: Add a bounded mutation-calibration stage before the existing staged activation-patching diagnosis. Use temporary diagnostic execution variants of each category’s single frozen NextItNet checkpoint to measure whether probes detect reachable readout, causality, and history-dependence faults.
idea.motivation: The existing adapter has extensive controls, but controls passing does not demonstrate detection power. Known diagnostic faults provide labeled challenges and unchanged executions provide false-alarm controls. This is feasible at early research progress and can prevent unsupported interpretation of later patch results.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve the actual trained view.model and all ModelView interfaces. Do not train, save, deploy, or combine mutated variants; they are temporary diagnostic executions sharing the same frozen weights, never additional predictors.

Cache at most two training-loader batches and select at most 16 uniquely identifiable training users per category with local seed 42. Reject ambiguous identities with counts. Use original aligned positives and negatives for score observations. Explicitly label all results as training diagnostics. Reserve at most 20 seconds within the existing 120-second category diagnostic budget; stop at the next operation boundary and report incomplete coverage.

Implement mutations through scoped diagnostic callables rather than editing checkpoint parameters or globally replacing public methods. The incorrect-readout mutation gathers count−1 only on nonempty left-padded examples where that index differs from the maximum occupied index. Establish reachability by observing a feature or score discrepancy against the correct reference. The future-access mutation explicitly mixes a later valid feature into an earlier valid position; compare paired inputs differing only at that later position. It is unreachable when no qualifying positions or nonzero observable change exist. The constant-feature mutation broadcasts a fixed diagnostic feature across histories; test different histories with the same candidate IDs. Measure whether the existing history-sensitivity alarm detects it, while recognizing that low sensitivity in the unmodified model is not itself proof of an implementation fault.

Predeclare feature and score tolerances, for example FP32 atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5. Reachability witnesses must be recorded separately from probe outputs; do not count a witness assertion as successful diagnostic detection. Evaluate fault-by-probe cells only when the injected behavior is observable under its declared stimulus. Report scheduled, executed, reachable, detected, false-alarm, and missing counts. Report per-fault rates with denominators; do not collapse faults into an unexplained health score. Label localization only for probes with predefined component labels; otherwise return null with a reason.

Run unchanged and identity-hook controls on the same examples. Save and restore per-module training modes, RNG/backend settings if modified, and all hooks in finally. If a control fails, invalidate affected calibration and patch results. A passed calibration supports only detection of these injected faults. It does not certify export parity, complete locality, useful personalization, or user suitability.

Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, four category routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Train exactly one independent NextItNet model per category. This diagnostic-only proposal leaves architecture and deployed inference unchanged, so checkpoint and embedded predictor remain consistent. Never access hidden tests or reconstruct pinned validation candidates.

originality.positive: Connects explicit NextItNet contract faults to staged patching interpretation through a fault-by-probe detection matrix.
originality.negative: Mutation testing and negative controls are established; novelty lies mainly in the task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable way to expose diagnostic blind spots before using interventions to motivate training changes.
future_potential.negative: Detection of a few artificial faults provides limited evidence about naturally occurring failures or validation improvement.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires bounded forward executions and scoped wrappers without retraining or changing deployed inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Independent reachability witnesses, nonrecursive wrappers, restoration, and meaningful detection denominators require careful implementation.

related_work.title: DeepCrime
contributions: Provides a foundation for mutation testing using faults grounded in deep-learning development errors.
limitations: Does not directly establish detection performance for this NextItNet diagnostic adapter.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Shows that activation-patching findings depend on corruption procedures and measurement choices.
limitations: Transfer to NextItNet recommendation models requires empirical assessment.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Demonstrates that sampled recommendation metrics can produce misleading model comparisons.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator or treating training diagnostic rankings as validation results.
